Today, we released SentinelBench, an open benchmark for agents whose main job is to wait. Most agent work assumes the agent has to keep acting to make progress. That breaks down for a big class of tasks. No amount of refreshing makes concert tickets go on sale faster. The right move is to watch, wait, and act only when the environment changes on its own. Today's agents are bad at this. They either churn on every page refresh, burning tokens and risking errors, or they give up after a few tries. SentinelBench measures exactly this. 100 tasks across 10 synthetic web apps (email, chat, a stock tracker, a music feed, and more) that evolve on their own timeline while the agent works. Some tasks are passive detection ("tell me when my post hits 100 likes"), some force the agent to keep checking, and 20 are designed to never fire, to catch agents that just declare success right before the clock runs out. How an agent waits can matter as much as which model you pick. A naive sleep-and-poll loop cost 5.1x more than a purpose-built wait_for tool at the 10-minute setting, with equal or worse accuracy. Stretch tasks to 40 minutes and the gap hits 9.7x. One sleep run cost $31 to finish a single task. As agents take on longer work, more of their time goes to waiting than acting. We think that deserves to be measured. Blog: https://lnkd.in/gjKvdTFh Code: https://lnkd.in/gR5msGCs ...more ...more

Excited to see this work come out of our Microsoft AI Frontiers research lab in collaboration with Matheus Kunzler Maldaner . Most agents today optimize for action. Reality is different — many tasks require waiting, monitoring, and acting at the right moment. SentinelBench is an important step toward evaluating this behavior. ...more

Today we're releasing SentinelBench, a benchmark for evaluating AI agents on long-horizon monitoring tasks! Working with Microsoft AI Frontiers , we created 10 synthetic web-app environments based on familiar apps like email, social media, video and music. The goal is to test how modern LLM-based agents perform on tasks that require them to wait, monitor and act only when the right condition is met. For example, if you ask an agent to "wait until Matheus' latest LinkedIn post reaches 50 likes and notify me," it would need to first find the post, then monitor it over time, and only respond at the right moment. Testing this on real websites is hard since do not control when events happen, pages may change layout, and providers may detect and block agent traffic. SentinelBench bypasses these issues, and we're open-sourcing it so other researchers can test their own agents or adapt the environments/scenarios for their own goals. This builds on work we started last summer on agents that can wait before acting. We had an initial agent-waiting strategy but could not measure its success without a controlled benchmark. SentinelBench was built to meet that need, and we improved the strategy along the way. Huge thank you to the team: Adam Fourney , Amanda Swearngin , Hussein Mozannar , Gagan Bansal , Maya Murad , Rafah Aboul Hosn and Saleema Amershi . It has been an extremely rewarding time working with Microsoft. P.S. I'll finish my master's this fall and will be applying for PhD programs. I'm also looking for research roles for the spring and summer terms, and would be grateful for any pointers :) Links to the GitHub, blog post and research write-up in the comments ...more

activity.title: 25 years at the University of Florida ! 🐊 My career has taken lots of turns since I first started! I began in the Botany Department (now Biology) and the Florida Museum of Natural History , managing the lab for Pam Soltis and Douglas Soltis , teaching, and helping many students, post-docs and visitors. Thank you to Pam and Doug for endless support! Over time, I drifted more toward computing, setting up the Soltis Lab's first cluster and growing to support the UF Genetic Institute's cluster. Now I work with UF Information Technology (UFIT) , training, teaching and supporting researchers using HiPerGator, one of the most powerful supercomputers in higher education! Overall, incredibly rewarding! Looking forward to more! #UniversityOfFlorida #ResearchComputing #CareerMilestone #HPC #UFIT

activity.title: Last week I had the chance of attending the Y Combinator Startup School! I got to watch speakers like Sam Altman, Jensen Huang , Chelsea Finn at the Chase Center; went to events at Google DeepMind ; met the most driven founders from 120 different countries; and got $25K in credits! As well, during our time in San Francisco, we learned from Mar Hershenson from Pear VC , Adeyemi Ajao from Base10 Partners , and Martin Casado from Andreessen Horowitz ; did a hackathon with Andrew Ng , met Dwarkesh Podcast Patel and watched Fei-Fei Li ; watched Spain become World Champions; and stayed in a Hacker House with Spanish builders we met through X! ( SOTI , The Exponential Fellowship ) We were able to learn from the best in the Startups and AI ecosystem and these are some of my takeaways: > Find something you have conviction in and stick with it, even against the odds. Sam Altman: OpenAI started with ~50 people worldwide who believed AGI was possible. Blake Scholl bet the same way on Boom, a supersonic aircraft company, with zero aerospace background. > Companies are just group of people with a mission. Company culture and hiring the right people are essential for growth. Max Junestrand from Legora interviewed every candidate up to 500 employees and flies every hire to Stockholm HQ. > Be intellectually fearless. Fei-Fei Li described her best students (Karpathy among others) with that phrase. Dwarkesh Patel never moves on without finding the answer to his question. Obsess with truth-seeking. > There's never been a better time to build. Patrick Collison : new businesses on Stripe are up ~2x year over year, the biggest jump ever recorded. Ade from Base10 backs it up: "it has never been a better time to raise money". And the overall motto: 𝗬𝗼𝘂 𝗰𝗮𝗻 𝗷𝘂𝘀𝘁 𝗱𝗼 𝘁𝗵𝗶𝗻𝗴𝘀. Don't ask for permission; just get started. The world around you wasn't built by people just accepting the status quo. Really impressed by the drive and courage of everybody I met. Shoutout to some really cool people I got to meet and hang out with ( Julian Abelarde , Oriol Pont , Tim Nguyen , Zach Derhake , Matheus Kunzler Maldaner , Pavan Kumar , Manuel Martín Morante , Noah van Lienden ). And thanks to marcos valera and Ignacio Moreno Pubul for giving chances to the Spanish Builders, inmense talent coming from home!

activity.title: Super excited to share that I'm joining Recursion as Chief AI Officer to lead end-to-end AI strategy and execution. Human biology stems from four billion years of evolution, which creates a proliferation of complexity and heterogeneity. Jensen Huang likened drug discovery as "wandering in the forest looking for truffles", which still vastly underestimated the challenge. The combinatorial explosion of biological hypotheses easily surpasses the number of atoms in the universe. Meanwhile, medical discovery advances at the snail pace of clinical trials, each taking years and costing over $100 million. As we enter the era of precision health and try to tailor treatments for each individual, continuing on today's discovery processes is clearly unsustainable. Since completing a PhD in machine learning and NLP, advancing AI for precision health has been my true north. In the past decade and half, I had the privilege of leading biomedical AI research at Microsoft, where our overarching agenda centered around creating a "virtual patient" as the high-fidelity digital twin by harnessing real-world data as a population-scale free lunch. We attained some baby steps from productivity gains to creativity gains, from reimagining drug development with agentic AI, to pretraining multimodal foundation models for patient stratification. But we also encountered two fundamental limitations: perturbation is restricted to approved interventions, and unraveling the underlying mechanism is plagued by a plethora of confounding factors. That is what drew me to Recursion. Personally, I can't think of a better use of AI than Recursion's mission of "decoding biology to radically improve lives". In the past decade, the Recursion team has built an impressive array of infrastructures across drug discovery and clinical development, operating one of the largest AI compute clusters in biopharma, and pioneering industrial-scale phenomics for perturbation data generation at single-cell resolution, long before "virtual cell" entered the mainstream. As Chief AI Officer, I'll lead the AI pursuit to unify frontier research and end-to-end applications across drug discovery and clinical development. We have an unprecedented opportunity to develop a unifying biomedical world model by bridging virtual patient and virtual cell, and turning real-world data into a discovery engine for prioritizing data acquisition in a generalized lab-in-the-loop flywheel. This in turn fuels diverse applications from imminent productivity gains via automating digitized knowledge work, to moonshot creativity gains via constructing biomedical wind tunnels for in silico simulation. By leveraging AI to close the loop across clinical care and early R&D, we have a clear line of sight toward scalable drug discovery. I'm grateful for the trust by Najat Khan, PhD and team. Can't wait to start working with the amazing team at Recursion to democratize precision health for everyone. Patients can't wait!
